Hi Anna / Marcus — thanks for the clear questions. Below is an implementation-focused proposal you can review; I kept it tight for procurement and your engineering team. Happy to expand on any section.

1) Latency target clarification
- The 150ms figure we called out is a per-token generation tail target for the streaming chat path. End-to-end user perception for a 512-token reply will of course be higher (roughly token-rate * token-count + network/processing). For planning assume ~2.5–3.5s for a 512-token generation under our low-latency config (higher variance on mobile networks). We’ll benchmark during the POC.

2) Routing & fallback chain (opinionated default)
- Primary route: high-quality model (rlhf-tuned open-varying checkpoint) on dedicated capacity in us-west (latency SLO).
- Secondary (fallback): quantized 8-bit variant of a similar architecture on cheaper GPU nodes (lower cost, slightly higher latency if warm).
- Tertiary (degraded mode): small, low-cost model for short answers / paraphrase only.
- Policy config knobs we recommend exposing: latency_target_ms (e.g., 150), cost_budget_per_request (USD cents), prefer_dedicated (boolean), region_preference (us-west/us-east), and max_fallback_depth.
- Example simplified routing policy (POC): {"priority": ["primary","secondary","tertiary"], "latency_target_ms": 150, "cost_budget_cents": 12} 
  - Note: We'll provide a JSON/YAML config file in the POC package (attached draft).

3) SDK & auth options
- Mobile streaming SDK: use short-lived tokens created by your backend (recommended) or mTLS for server-to-server critical endpoints. Short-lived tokens + refresh flow reduces key leakage risk for native apps.
- Backend/batch: server API keys or mTLS; for PHI we recommend mTLS + customer-managed KMS for key wrapping at rest.
- We can provide an example authentication flow using our SDK (Node/Python) that shows token exchange and token scoping by route/model.

4) Embeddings & reranker design
- Nightly batch embedding job: use chunking at ~768 tokens and batch size tuned to your GPU memory. Prefer asynchronous bulk endpoint and use prefix caching for repeat doc segments.
- For 2M docs: shard the embedding jobs by date/namespace; expect throughput of ~3–4K docs/min on a dedicated 16GB GPU node depending on model. We'll provide cost estimates in the POC.
- Reranker at query time: two-stage retrieval — ANN candidate generation (FAISS/HNSW in your infra) followed by a light reranker on a smaller but high-quality model. Reranker can run with a 100–200ms tail SLO if served on dedicated small instances.

5) Structured output & tool calling
- For discharge-summary tagging and automated field extraction, enable structured output schema enforcement in the SDK and use tool-calls for DB writes. We suggest output-validated JSON schema + a sandboxed tool that writes updates to your EHR staging tables (idempotent design).

6) Caching, KV, and cost controls
- Prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts (triage templates) will reduce token costs by up to 30% on warm paths.
- Configure autoscaling with a burst policy to maintain latency SLOs and a cost cap to prevent runaway spend.

POC deliverables we propose:
- Routing config draft (JSON + YAML) + benchmark script.
- SDK quickstart (Node + iOS streaming snippet).
- Embedding job template + reranker config and cost estimate.
- Short security packet for procurement (KMS, SOC2 references).

I attached the draft routing proposal and a simple architecture diagram for your engs to review. Proposed timing: 2-week POC, with initial benchmarks in 4–5 business days once we have sample data and a signed POC NDA.

Next steps: can you confirm (a) a target date for the tech kickoff, (b) who will own sample data upload, and (c) the procurement contact?
